biblical_reference.note: Antipas was a martyr in Pergamos, where he stood for his faith in Jesus Christ during the Roman Empire period.

saint_reference.note: Saint Antipas of Pergamos, a martyr and disciple of Jesus Christ, is mentioned in the Book of Revelation as one of the seven churches in Asia.

data.cultural_impact: Antipas was the name of King Herod Antipas, who ruled over Galilee and Perea from 4 BC to 39 AD. He is most famously known for executing John the Baptist on a trumped-up charge of sedition. Antipas' name became synonymous with a political and religious leader who was intolerant of opposing views, particularly against those espousing the new monotheistic faith of Christianity.
data.spiritual_significance: In the New Testament, the name Antipas is given to three other individuals who opposed the teachings of Jesus and the early Christian church. Antipas, one of the Synagogue rulers, challenged Jesus to work a miracle to heal a man born blind (John 9:1-41). Another Antipas, an Arabian ruler, is mentioned in the New Testament book of Revelation as one of the enemies of God Almighty (Revelation 2:13). The name Antipas also appears in the apocryphal account of the martyrdom of St. Peter, in which Antipas is said to have ordered Peter's execution in Rome. Antipas, in these spiritual contexts, represents the opposition and persecution that early Christians faced as they spread the teachings of Jesus.
